thought.text: The prompt hung because stdin was closed (I omitted `URBO_INSTANCE`). Let me persist the instance identifier as the tool would, and re-run.

reasoning_content:
Interesting: "Instance identifier [workspace]:" prompt appeared, and then "Detected unsettled top-level await" — process was killed by timeout? No wait — exit code 13, "unsettled top-level await". What actually happened: even though I set URBO_INSTANCE... no wait! I didn't set URBO_INSTANCE in that command! Looking at the command: `export GITHUB_TOKEN=... && nohup just up --detach`. I forgot URBO_INSTANCE. But a prompt appeared... "Instance identifier [workspace]:" — it prompted and waited on stdin (nohup's stdin is /dev/null? actually nohup redirects stdin from /dev/null in bash? no — nohup doesn't redirect stdin. In a nohup background job with stdin being a terminal, readline should hang waiting for input...

Hmm, "Detected unsettled top-level await" is the Node warning at exit when the process was killed (exit code 13 = 128+? no, 13 isn't a signal... exit 13). Maybe readline closed immediately (stdin = /dev/null → immediate EOF → prompt returned '' → default 'workspace' used). Actually that would be the expected flow: prompt answered with '' → fallback to 'workspace' → continue.

But the process exited with 13 and "unsettled top-level await" — the promise was never resolved. When stdin closed, did createInterface throw an exception? Or was the process killed by my nohup... wait — "Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await" appears when the event loop empties while awaiting is still pending. The readline question was pending, and stdin closed → the question never resolves → but then the process should just hang... Actually when stdin emits 'close', readline's question callback isn't called, the promise stays pending, the event loop empties, and Node exits with the unsettled-top-level-await warning. Exit code 13.

So the problem: stdin was closed (no terminal) → prompt hung → exit 13.

Fix: pass URBO_INSTANCE=workspace explicitly in the env. That way resolveIdentifier won't prompt. Note that .urbo/workspace/ already exists from a previous partial run — and .urbo-instance? The previous successful dummy run was using envValue URBO_INSTANCE=workspace (never persisted, because "override is meant for a single run"). So .urbo-instance doesn't exist in the repo. For persistence, set URBO_INSTANCE in every subsequent command, or just write the .urbo-instance file. Better: write 'workspace\n' to /workspace/.urbo-instance — that's exactly what the tool does, and it makes `just up` work naturally from then on (and matches the guide's behavior "remembers it in .urbo-instance").

action.command:
cd /workspace && printf 'workspace\n' > .urbo-instance && cat .urbo-instance && export GITHUB_TOKEN="urbo-dev-token-not-consumed-by-build" && nohup just up --detach > /tmp/just-up-final.log 2>&1 &
echo "just up pid $!"; sleep 45; tail -15 /tmp/just-up-final.log; pgrep -f up.mjs >/dev/null && echo RUNNING || echo DONE

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && printf 'workspace\\n' > .urbo-instance && cat .urbo-instance && export GITHUB_TOKEN=\"urbo-dev-token-not-consumed-by-build\" && nohup just up --detach > /tmp/just-up-final.log 2>&1 &\necho \"just up pid $!\"; sleep 45; tail -15 /tmp/just-up-final.log; pgrep -f up.mjs >/dev/null && echo RUNNING || echo DONE", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Persist instance id and run just up --detach"}

summary: Persist instance id and run just up --detach
